subject: Urban Planning
title: Euclidean Zoning: The American Model
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Euclidean Zoning: The American Model.

hook.text: In 1926, the Supreme Court upheld zoning in Village of Euclid v. Ambler. It created the system America still uses.

buildup.text: Euclidean zoning separates land into residential, commercial, and industrial districts. Each zone has strict rules.

discovery.text: You can't build a shop in a residential zone or an apartment above a store. Every use is separated by law.

twist.text: This separation created car dependency — you drive to work, drive to shop, drive to eat. Nothing is nearby.

climax.text: Most walkable cities predate Euclidean zoning. The mixed-use neighborhoods people love are now mostly illegal to build.

punchline.text: The neighborhood you love? Probably illegal under current zoning.

quiz.question: What did Euclidean zoning separate?
options: Building heights from lot sizes based on traffic density
Land into residential, commercial, and industrial districts
Public land from private land based on tax revenue
